bible.title: Meridian Sanctuary
bible.intent:
A bright, sunlit sanctuary of ivory marble that floats above a sea of cloud. One long axis runs from the arrival, along a marble causeway between still turquoise reflecting pools, up shallow terraces and stairs, to a colossal arched gateway with a mirror orb hanging in its opening. Arcades, pillars and stairways frame the axis; thin waterfalls slip from planted ledges into the pools; cypresses rise from marble planters and ivy trails from every arch. Brushed brass lines the paths and pool edges, and narrow slots in the stone glow with warm light.

Overhead, the sanctuary repeats itself upside down: terraces, arches and cascades hang from the sky like a reflection with no water, and polished cubes drift at every scale, from a block you could almost touch to monoliths the size of buildings far out over the clouds. Gravity is the illusion; the ground is the truth. Under your feet everything is calm, level and legible, and the strangeness lives above and beyond the rim.

It should feel serene, warm, vast and slightly impossible, like walking through a memory of noon. Never dark, never neon, never a backrooms corridor.
bible.rules:
1. Bright first. Ivory and white marble, turquoise water, deep green planting and golden light. No dark, neon, fluorescent or backrooms reading from any view.
2. One axis. The central gateway is the visual anchor: the tallest grounded structure by a clear margin, standing on the main axis at its far end. Its arch and orb stay in unbroken view at eye height from every check view: the arrival, the middle of the causeway, the head of every flight and the cove.
3. Route before ornament. A continuous walkable route runs from the arrival along the causeway, around the pool edges, up stairs to each terrace and through the gateway threshold. It is walked, never jumped or waded: no step taller than a stair riser and no gap a walker can drop through. Plan routes, landings and sightlines before decoration, and check them in the world by walking them.
4. Human scale underfoot. Steps about 0.15–0.18 m high and 0.3–0.4 m deep, no more than twelve risers between landings, and landings at least 1.5 m deep. Pool copings about 0.4 m wide with the water a hand's width below them; planters and balustrades about 0.6–1.1 m high, so they read against a 1.7 m walker.
5. Ground is truth, sky is the dream. Everything walkable is grounded and continuous. Floating cubes, inverted architecture and any upward water live overhead or beyond the rim: never above the route, never closer than 1.5 m to anything walkable, and never across the gateway's silhouette from a check view, so the nearest block is one you could almost touch. Visual only: no working portals or gravity changes in this version.
6. A ladder of scale. Every check view holds at least three readable scales: human details near (planters, copings, steps), monumental arcades and the gateway in the middle, colossal floating forms far away and softened by haze.
7. Water. Still, clear turquoise pools over pale marble floors with caustic light, shallow enough to wade and never deep enough to swim; the surface mirrors the sky. Thin waterfalls and overflowing edges feed the pools, and at the sanctuary's rim, in view of the arrival, water spills into the cloud sea.
8. Stone. Two marbles: warm, pitted ivory travertine for walls, piers and structure; white veined marble for floors, copings and stairs. Crisp monolithic blocks with small bevels and visible joints, never plastic. Brushed brass only as thin inlays and trims.
9. Planting. Tall columnar cypress in marble planters, low flowering shrubs and trailing ivy. Planting frames the axis in pairs but varies in height and fullness so it never reads as copy-paste.
10. Light. A high golden sun, about 35–50° above the horizon and on your left as you walk toward the gateway, gives soft, long shadows and warm bounce on ivory. Lit slots in walls and the gateway's inner arch glow warm white, never coloured.
11. Mirrors. The orb in the gateway and the floating cubes are polished and reflect sky and cloud. Cubes drift or turn slowly: no bob quicker than half a minute and no turn faster than once a minute. Nothing moves fast.
12. Sky and beyond. A deep blue zenith fading to a luminous warm haze, with tall soft cumulus. There is no ground below the sanctuary, only a sea of clouds: foundations and falling water dissolve into it, and no terrain shows beyond the rim.
13. Symmetry with life. The main court is bilaterally symmetric about the axis; far architecture and floating forms break that symmetry so the world feels found, not generated.
14. The cove stays at the origin as the maker space, beside the composition rather than on the axis. It is one of the check views, so the gateway's arch and orb are in view from inside it.
15. References are inspiration. The hero image sets the direction; the other images are AI-generated concepts, not measured plans or texture maps. Keep measured results separate from concepts and targets.
16. Budget. Keep real headroom on every cap: at least eight asset slots, two hundred placements and a fifth of the triangle budget free. Keep both renderer backends refresh-paced on the hub GPU, where draws are usually the binding cost, and measure it in the world rather than estimating.
